catalog_quote: [p.446 sec.5.0] The marker of the direct case is zero in the singular and stressed -ə in the plural. The marker of the oblique is stressed -ə in the singular and stressed -un/-on in the plural; e.g., zumu/vay uma 'the groom/the bride came' ... [p.448 sec.7.1] The adjective precedes the noun it modifies which is connected to the adjective by an unstressed -e (the stress falling on the noun); e.g., āl-e āsb 'red horse', zārd-e karg 'yellow hen' ... [p.449 n.7] In ave, ame, and šeme the accent falls on the second syllable. [p.450 sec.8.5] Demonstrative pronouns are also used as personal pronouns. The stress falls on the last syllable. [p.454 sec.16.0] Negative of the above: 1. nine, 2. niše, 3. nie, 4. nimbe, 5. ninie, 6. ninde (the stress falls on ni-). ... c) From the stem bav-: ... Preterit: 1. bine, 2. biše, 3. bie, 4. bimbe, 5. binye, 6. binde (the stress falls on the first syllable). [p.459 sec.24.0] The imperfect is built with the stem II by adding a stressed -e to it followed by the preterit of the verb 'to be'. ... [p.459 sec.25.0] The perfect is built with the stem II and the perfect marker, stressed -ā.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No general word-stress rule is stated. Every located statement puts stress on the last syllable of the (inflected) nominal word: the case/number suffixes -ə, -un/-on carry the stress, the disyllabic personal and demonstrative pronouns are end-stressed, and the adjectival linker -e is an unstressed enclitic with stress staying on the noun. In the verb, stress is morphologically placed (stressed tense formants -e, -a after stem II; negative ni- of the copula attracts stress). Reading 'fixed: final syllable' is therefore an inference from consistent morpheme-level statements, not an explicit rule of the author.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed adjectival connective -e (stress on following noun); negative copula stressed on prefix ni-; preterit marker -i- unstressed with stress on last syllable of the stem (stated for Kalasuri, Yarshater 2005:275-276); verb forms stress the tense formant rather than the final personal ending.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern individual word classes/morphemes in elicited words and sentences (fieldwork 1960s-70s, informant Ali Beyrami, Karingan village). The Kalasur/Khoynarud sketch (Yarshater 2005) gives the parallel morpheme-level facts for the Kalasuri-Khoynarudi half of the glottocode. Neither sketch has a 'Stress' paragraph in its Phonology section (checked on the pages themselves).
new_statements.identity_note: Yarshater 2007 describes the dialect of Karingan village (Karingani/Kerengani proper, Varzaqan district); Yarshater 2005, Asghari 2006/2008, Mowlaei 2016 and Sabzalipour 2011 describe the closely related dialect of Kalasur and Khoynarud (Kaleybar district). Glottolog 5.1 subsumes all three under kari1303 'Karingani-Kalasuri-Khoynarudi' (ISO kgn); the quoted statement is from the Karingan variety, with parallel morpheme-level stress facts for Kalasuri in Yarshater 2005 (pp. 271-280). Karang 1954's 'Tati' is also the Karingan dialect (his 'Harzani' = Harzandi, a different glottocode).

sources.citation: Mowlaei, Changiz (1395/2016). Fe'l dar guyesh-e Kalasuri [Verb system in Kalasuri dialect]. Zaban-e Farsi va Guyesh-ha-ye Irani (Univ. of Guilan) 1(2): 43-65.
sources.note: Abstract (clean HTML): intransitive simple past and present perfect are formally identical and 'distinguished by the position of stress' (tamayoz-e in do fe'l az jaygah-e takye). Decodable body passage (p.~55): in the simple past stress is on the final syllable of the past stem, in the perfect on the perfect-stem morpheme; cites Yarshater 1969:197, 227-229 for the same rule in Southern Tati. Verb-internal stress only; no general word-stress rule.
